claim: The Chamber of Deputies completes the second reading of the 2027 state budget bill (print 324) on Wednesday 25 November 2026.

runs.reason:
**Base rate.** The two comparable cases I checked both completed second reading in a single sitting day: the 2024 budget on November 15, 2023, and the 2026 budget on March 4, 2026. That’s a 2-for-2 benchmark, not a large enough sample to treat same-day completion as a certainty. ([psp.cz](https://www.psp.cz/eknih/2021ps/stenprot/082schuz/82-2.html))

**What moves this case.** **Up:** ČT24 on November 20 and ČTK on November 22 both identified Wednesday, November 25 as the second-reading day. ČTK’s report was based on coalition plans conveyed by Chamber Speaker Tomio Okamura. **Up:** The Budget Committee had already recommended approval on November 11, so committee work was not holding up the floor debate. **Down:** This bill’s first reading ran across October 21 and 22, and MPs were still filing amendments on November 23. That makes a spillover more plausible, although second reading cannot reopen the budget’s basic totals. ([ct24.ceskatelevize.cz](https://ct24.ceskatelevize.cz/clanek/ekonomika/jak-zlepsit-verejne-finance-experti-navrhuji-upravy-v-danich-i-revizi-vydaju-379736))

**Window risk.** I put about 3% on the reading not opening on November 25 and another 8% on it opening without reaching formal closure that day. The larger risk is a debate that runs long or is suspended, not a last-minute change to the start date. ([blesk.cz](https://www.blesk.cz/clanek/zpravy-politika/853234/poslanci-se-v-tydnu-vrati-ke-spornemu-snizeni-podpor-i-mimoradne-dani-na-rafinerie.html?utm_source=openai))

runs.reason:
The second reading of a Czech state-budget bill is usually finished in one long sitting when the Chamber gives it a full day that starts in the morning. Under this coalition the second reading of the 2026 budget took about twelve hours; the 2025 second reading was also closed in a single day. First readings run longer and more often spill into a second calendar day.

The official timetable adopted in September assigns the second reading of print 324 to 25 November 2026 and the third reading to the sitting that opens on 2 December, which only works cleanly if the second reading ends with the statutory 48-hour gap intact. The draft order of the 37th session places that second reading as the first item on Wednesday, and the sitting is set to resume at 09:00. On 22 November ČTK, citing the Speaker, reported that the Chamber will take up the budget in second reading on Wednesday. The coalition has a working majority and has already used night sittings on this bill. Those facts pull toward a close on the 25th.

The same bill’s first reading was also calendared for a single day and still ran 19.5 hours across 21–22 October after opposition club breaks. Twenty-six written debate registrations are already logged, and Thursday’s order has fixed interpellation slots at 11:00 and 14:30, so an unfinished debate is easy to adjourn rather than force past midnight.

This reform restricts debate on agenda modifications and expands the Chamber majority's power to limit speaking times—including for speakers with priority speaking rights—and to set fixed voting or debate-closing times. Furthermore, because the budget's second reading is scheduled according to the mandatory statutory budget timetable, it is not delayed by opening agenda-modification debates once its slot arrives.
* **Precedent from the March 2026 budget reading under the same government (Moves toward YES):** On 4 March 2026, the exact same governing coalition (ANO, SPD, Motoristé) and opposition completed the second reading of the 2026 state budget (print 94) within 12 hours on a single Wednesday (from 9:00 AM to around 9:00 PM).
* **Heightened opposition willingness to obstruct the 2027 budget (Moves toward NO):** During the first reading of print 324 on 21–22 October 2026, opposition parties extended the debate over two days (unlike the typically single-day first reading), prompting coalition deputies to remark on 22 October 2026 that the opposition was obstructing the state budget for the first time in history. Additionally, high political tension persists over the 386 billion CZK deficit and public media financing.

### 3. Strongest Reason the Obvious Outcome Might Fail
Even with the amended Rules of Procedure and a 9:00 AM start on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, the second reading requires completing both the general debate (*obecná rozprava*) and the detailed debate (*podrobná rozprava*, in which deputies formally read out their reallocation proposals). If opposition clubs (ODS, STAN, Pirates, KDU-ČSL, TOP 09) coordinate an unusually large volume of reallocation amendments and use their speaking allowances and two-minute factual remarks (*faktické poznámky*, which were largely preserved in the Rules of Procedure reform) to the maximum, the debate could stretch past 15 hours. In that scenario, either the session could spill past 23:59 into the early morning hours of Thursday, 26 November 2026 (similar to the first reading of the public media bill on 23–24 October 2026, which ended at 4:36 AM), or the presiding officer could adjourn the debate around midnight to resume on Thursday morning.

Balancing the strong historical precedent of single-day completion, the 9:00 AM priority slot, and the newly enacted procedural tools available to the governing majority against the risk of a post-midnight spillover or overnight adjournment, I estimate an 85% probability that the second reading closes before 23:59 on Wednesday, 25 November 2026.
